BBC: Labour sees off Green challenge to win Holborn by-election. By Alicia Curry. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-09T02:06:35Z (03:06 BST); dateModified 09:32Z (10:32 BST).
Sagal Abdi-Wali (Camden council leader) held the seat for Labour; majority cut from 11,572 to 3,364. Lab 45%, Green 33%. Green share up 22 points on GE2024. Ewan Cameron (Con) third, 1,922 (7%), then Reform UK, Lib Dems, Restore Britain.
Abdi-Wali: 'People voted for hope and now we're going to be able to deliver for them.'
Abdi-Wali: 'I hope this moment also says something about who gets to belong, for people who look like me, I hope they see themselves reflected in this place and know that their path too belongs here. This is Camden, and this is Britain.'
Abdi-Wali: 'Winning not by making people afraid of each other, but by bringing people together.'
Abdi-Wali at rally with deputy leader Lucy Powell: homelessness was 'the thing that drove me into politics'; rough sleepers should 'know we have their backs'. Wants Thames Water in public ownership, saying it 'failed residents up and down our constituency'.
PM Andy Burnham congratulated her on a 'fantastic campaign'. Keir Starmer: 'I know you are a brilliant champion for our communities and will be a fantastic MP.'
Polanski to BBC Radio 4 Today: 'I'm not going to sit here and pretend I'm not disappointed. No politician runs in a by-election and doesn't want to win.' / 'to see the growth in what was supposedly a safe Labour seat since 1983 [and] is now a marginal Labour seat, that's clearly growth and next time we can get it over the line.' Calls it 'our second best by-election result in Green Party history'.
Polanski: 'Of course I can carry on as leader of the Green Party.' Voters 'excited about our plans for rent controls, tackling the climate crisis and nationalising Thames Water'.
Caroline Lucas (former Green leader) to BBC: Polanski failed to show leadership; motion 'dangerous' and 'divisive'. Asked if he should stand down: 'I think let's just see what happens in the coming days and weeks... I want him to show the leadership that was frankly missing on Sunday. I think the jury is out about whether he will do that - but I very much hope he will.'
Seat Labour since creation in 1983, 40%+ at every general election.
